phase: Phase 1: Allow list in the guard
summary: The allow list of Decision 3 to 11 resists every adversarial probe. All 12 mutation classes are rejected by a test, except X2 as written, which is a no-op; an effective X2 form is rejected by B5 and V11. The 19 new adversarial cases are committed at c59ee94 in plugins/opencode-measure-guard/tests/allow-adversarial.test.ts. The plugin suite gives 131 pass and 0 fail, the mod suite 91 pass and 0 fail, tsc exits 0, parity is ok, and the review gate gives 10 suites. Two nonblocking items remain: the O(n*n) dedupe cost, and the no-op X2 mutation text.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Nit] test-strategy.md section 4.6 (X2): the X2 mutation as written is a no-op. isAllowed already calls joinPath on both sides, and isInside calls joinPath again, so skipping the second joinPath changes no result. Probe X2-literal ran 46 tests and caught nothing. The effective form (raw segment compare with no resolution) is caught by B5 and V11. Rationale: this is a defect in the mutation list, not in the shipped code; the strategy asks X2 to prove path resolution, and only the effective form proves it.

F2 [Nit] plugins/opencode-measure-guard/src/core/parse.ts:54 (parseAllowList): the dedupe uses folders.includes in a forEach, so the cost is O(n*n). A 50 000-line list with 50 000 unique entries takes 7 981 ms to parse (probe P9). loadSnapshot runs at each guarded tool call. The agent can write measure/guard-allow (the accepted residual risk of Decision 15), so an agent can add seconds to each of its own calls. Rationale: the list never allows a wrong path, so this is availability only; the operator owns the file.
